comments.text: The pole vault's picture, a multicolour bitmap in VIC bank 1 ($4000-$5F3F): sky and clouds, the crowded stands with their flags, the runway in the infield and, on the right, the uprights and the blue landing mat. Character rows 0-2
Pole vault bitmap, character rows 3-5: clouds
Pole vault bitmap, character rows 6-8: the tops of the uprights
Pole vault bitmap, character rows 9-11: the stands with flags
Pole vault bitmap, character rows 12-14: the front of the stands and the infield
Pole vault bitmap, character rows 15-17: the infield and the runway
Pole vault bitmap, character rows 18-20: the runway and the landing mat
Pole vault bitmap, character rows 21-23: the foot of the mat and the grass
Bitmap row 24, the text line: clear_text fills it with set bits and draw_char writes letters into it
The last 64 bytes of the text line's bitmap, filled by clear_text
The 192 bytes between the bitmap and $6000, which the VIC never shows
The picture's colour RAM, copied to $D800 by setup_screen ($BC96): rows 0-6
The picture's colour RAM, rows 6-12, copied to $D900
The picture's colour RAM, rows 12-19, copied to $DA00
The picture's colour RAM, rows 19-24, copied to $DB00, with 24 spare bytes
Screen RAM of the picture ($6400-$67E7, $D018 = $90): in multicolour bitmap mode each byte holds two colours of its cell. Rows 0-12
Screen colours of the picture, rows 13-24
The colour cells of the text line, row 24: draw_char sets each letter's colour here and clear_text blanks them
The last cell of the text line's colours, which show_message sets from msg_end_colour
The eight sprite pointers, $A0-$A7: each sprite shows its own 64-byte buffer from $6800, into which the code copies the shape it needs

Zero bytes up to the module's entry, nothing in them
More zero bytes before the module's entry at $6FE0

The module's entry (module 3, file D), from the engine's loader: sets the processor port so BASIC is out and the KERNAL and I/O in, which leaves the RAM at $A000-$BFFF for the event's code, then jumps to pv_start
Zero bytes before the shapes
The vaulter's shapes, $C0-$EE ($7000-$7BBF), copied into the sprites by copy_shape_lo: head and arms on the pole, legs in the run and in the swing, the body bent over the bar and lying on the mat
Vaulter shapes $D0-$DF: the running legs ($DE-$E4 by stride frame) and the swing
Vaulter shapes $E0-$EE: the end of the run, the push off the pole, and the landing on the mat
Zero bytes after the vaulter's shapes, up to the pole shapes at $8000
The last 64 zero bytes before the pole shapes at $8000

The pole's shapes, $00-$CE above $8000 ($8000-$B3BF), copied by copy_shape_hi: the pole as straight and bent lines at every angle from leaning forward to upright, three pieces to each position, in the order pole_pieces picks them
Pole shapes from $10: the pole lowered towards the box
Pole shapes from $20
Pole shapes from $30: the pole nearly flat
Pole shapes from $40: the pole planted and starting to bend
Pole shapes from $50: the bend
Pole shapes from $60: the bend deepening
Pole shapes from $70: the deepest bend
Pole shapes from $80: the pole straightening as it swings up
Pole shapes from $90: near upright
Pole shapes from $A0: upright
Pole shapes from $B0: the pole falling away forward
Pole shapes from $C0, to the last pole shape at $B380
Shape $CF: two thin upright bars, copied into sprite 0 by setup_screen

The crossbar's shapes, $D0-$D9 ($B400-$B67F): the bar lying flat and at steeper and steeper angles as it falls; bar_step chooses one by the bar's height, eight further on while it is still on the pegs

The pole vault's start: seeds its random generator from the CIA timer, shuffles the vaulting order at $C991 among the players, sets the starting height (the lowest, or the second in practice) and every player's result to FAULT, clears the text line
Finds the next player in the order still in at this height (attempt count 1-3); when nobody is, raises the bar ($C1EA) and starts again. In practice the one player goes at once

Sets up one attempt: interrupts, picture, SID; the bar at the height's place; clears the attempt's variables; medium grip; marks the attempt good until the bar falls; prints the name and the height. Then waits with interrupts on, and after a cleared vault plays the crowd's cheer
Waits for a vault to be cleared (vault_done set)
The crowd's cheer after a good vault: noise on voices 2 and 3, swept up and down for three bursts of 81 frames, then waits in a loop for ever while the interrupt goes on
The endless loop the main program ends in: everything goes on in the raster interrupt

The raster interrupt at line $D5: re-arms pv_irq2 at line $57, waits for line $DA, counts frames, and runs one step of the state machine through the table at $C903 (states 0-7 by $C9AA), jumping through an address it writes into its own JMP at $B7F4
The JMP whose address pv_irq writes from the state table
Low byte of the state routine's address, written by pv_irq
High byte of the state routine's address

State 5, the vault, one frame. Before the plant: pulling the stick down (bit 1 of $DC00) lowers the pole; from then the pole's position $C96E advances by the speed, and the runner moves one pixel a frame whatever happens. At position 31 the pole is planted: if the vaulter is short of the box (X below $80 with bit 8 clear) it is a fault; otherwise the speed is set by how far past $96 the plant was. A vaulter who reaches X $96 with the pole not yet planted faults
The run: places the running vaulter's three sprites, steps the stride every four frames with a footstep sound at stride 0, and draws the pole lowering as it is carried
Low byte of the carry table's address, set from carry_lo by the grip
High byte of the carry table's address, from carry_hi. Then the pole is drawn at its carried height, and the vaulter's three sprites are placed above the runner's position

On the pole: the vaulter follows the grip's trajectory tables. Pushing the stick up starts the swing, and the speed adds to the bend of the pole (frames 0-6); the button at the last bend frame lets go and starts the flight. The speed drains a little each frame by the bend frame ($C500)
Lets go of the pole: the flight's forward speed is half the speed plus $47, its upward speed an eighth of it
Draws the vaulter in the swing (three sprites from vault_pose) and the pole

The flight: moves the vaulter forward twice a frame by the forward speed and up or down by the vertical speed, which gravity increases each frame. Landing on the mat (Y $D4) bumps once with a thud and then lies still for a while in four landing poses

Draws the vaulter in the air or on the mat with the pole, then checks for the end: when the landing count runs out the vault is over; over the bar it is good, short of it (X below $15 past the 256 line) a fault
Goes on to the next frame's end
The attempt failed: clears the good-vault flag

The vault is over (state 5 to 6): clears the text line, prints the name, the height and FAILED ATTEMPT or GOOD VAULT. A good vault sets the player's count to 0 (through to the next height) and writes the height as the result ("x.y0M") and its number as the score; a failure counts a try, and a third failure puts the player out ($FF)
Waits for raster line $F4 and turns multicolour off for the text line, then back on at line $FB
State 6: the result is shown; the button moves on to the next vaulter, or in practice to state 7
State 7, practice: "ANOTHER JUMP? Y" or "N", chosen by the stick (up Y, down N) or the keys Y and N; the button jumps again, or leaves the event through $0900
Every frame's end: moves the falling bar; a speed of $F0 or more halves the speed and fails the vault; then leaves the interrupt
Pulls Y, X and A and returns from the interrupt
The second raster interrupt, at line $57: acknowledges it and re-arms pv_irq at line $D5
Turns off the CIA's interrupts, sets bitmap mode ($D011 = $3B), multicolour, and the raster interrupt at line $FB through pv_irq

The picture and the sprites: white background, black border, VIC bank 1 with the bitmap at $4000 and the screen at $6400, the colour RAM from $6000; the sprites' colours, expansion and multicolour (sprites 0 and 7), the pointers $A0-$A7, the bar's place, and the upright in sprite 0
The event's random generator, the engine's shift register with its two bytes in $18/$19
Copies shape A from $8000 + 64 x A into sprite Y's buffer: the pole and bar shapes
Copies shape A from $4000 + 64 x A into sprite Y's buffer: the vaulter's shapes
Sets sprite X/2's X from the vaulter's X and the grip's offset, flipping its bit 8 on a carry

Places sprite Y/2 as pole piece X: its doubling from pole_flags, its Y from pole_dy (with the stride's bob while running) and its X from pole_dx, from the vaulter's X while running and from the box ($8A) once planted
Places sprite Y as part X of the vaulter's pose from vault_pose: shape, and X and Y offsets from the vaulter
Clears the text line: black colours, every bitmap bit set

Draws character A in cell X of the text line in colour Y: copies seven rows of the letter from the character ROM's second set ($D800, seen by clearing bit 2 of $01) one pixel down into the bitmap at $5E00
Prints the vaulter's 16-character name from the player record at the start of the text line
Low byte of the player record's address, set to the vaulter's number times 32
Prints the bar's height, "x.y0M", at cells 18-22 of the text line

Moves the bar (sprite 7): while it falls, X and Y change by their speeds and it bounces off the ground with a thud; picks its shape by height. In the vault, a collision of the bar with the vaulter or pole knocks it: the attempt is failed and the bar falls. Also keeps sprite 0, the upright's top, level with the highest of the bar and the vaulter
The button, or RETURN: Z set on a new press
Joystick direction X (0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 button) in port 2: Z set on a new press, with a 15-frame repeat
Sprite roles for the vault and flight: which sprite is which pole piece and body part, and their colours
Sprite roles for the run
Prints message X, 16 characters, at the right of the text line in its colour
The LDA whose address show_message writes from msg_addr_lo/hi
Low byte of the message's address, set from msg_addr_lo
High byte of the message's address, set from msg_addr_hi
State 0: in practice, choose the height (state 0b at $C0A4); otherwise "NEW HEIGHT" on a player's first try at a height, waiting for the button, or straight to state 2 for a later try
Practice: "SET BAR HEIGHT", up and down move the bar through the heights, the button goes on to the grip
State 1: below 5.00 m asks "TRY THIS JUMP? Y/N"; N passes the height (the player waits for the next one)
State 2: "1ST TRY", "2ND TRY" or "LAST TRY", then the button
State 3: "SELECT POLE GRIP": up and down, or the keys H, M and L, choose a high, medium or low grip, which sets the starting speed; the button goes on once a choice has been made
State 4: "READY TO JUMP"; the button clears the line and starts the vault
Raises the bar one height and gives everyone still in (count 0) a first try; when nobody is left the event ends through $0900
The starting height, every attempt count 0, and every player's result " FAULT" with a score of 0
Tests RETURN

Tests key X of key_rows/key_cols (RETURN, Y, N, L, M, H) by driving its row low on $DC00 and reading its column on $DC01, ignoring it when a joystick is pulling the lines; C set on a new press, with a repeat delay
A footstep: a short burst of noise on voice 1
The bar's thud on the ground: a low pulse on voice 1
The vaulter landing on the mat: noise on voice 2
Code nothing calls: switches to text mode with the screen at $0400, puts video bank 0 in and jumps to $9000
Loads all 25 SID registers from sid_init
The SID's 25 registers at the start of each attempt: pulse width $0800 for the three voices and full volume, the rest zero

The runner's bob in height for each stride frame

High bytes of the grips' carry tables

vault_pose read from its fourth byte, the X offsets
vault_pose read from its seventh byte, the Y offsets
The vaulter's X on the pole for each position, with the high grip, read from position 31 on; the bytes before that are vault_pose's

The vaulter's X on the pole, medium grip
The vaulter's height on the pole, medium grip

How much speed each bend frame of the pole takes away each frame: 0 to $C0

Each sprite's bit inverted, twice over
For each pole piece: bit 0 doubles the sprite's width, bit 1 its height (and raises it)
For each pole piece, its height above the base line
For each pole piece, its X offset

N, 1ST TRY, 2ND TRY, LAST TRY, HIGH POLE GRIP, MED. POLE GRIP, LOW POLE GRIP, NEW HEIGHT, READY TO JUMP, SELECT POLE GRIP, SET BAR HEIGHT, ANOTHER JUMP? Y, ANOTHER JUMP? N
